models.note: 62 services; RCPs never restrict resources in the management account, calls by service-linked roles, AWS managed KMS keys or kms:RetireGrant

access through a share ends when the account leaves the organization or the OU the share is addressed to, unless the share was created with RetainSharingOnAccountLeaveOrganization for the account itself; what happens to traffic already flowing is modelled per resource type (transit gateways and subnets keep existing attachments and resources working, Resolver rules stop answering, others unverified)

Removing a member account: standalone-account information (verified contact details, payment method, support plan) or ConstraintViolationException; created accounts wait four days; no delegated administrator; tags deleted; the role Organizations created is kept; cost data stays with the management account. Invitations: one organization at a time, 15 days to answer, root and OU policies apply at once on acceptance, the organization trail applies automatically, OrganizationAccountAccessRole is not created for invited accounts. Management account: leaves only by deleting the organization after every member is removed, which deletes every organization policy; a Control Tower landing zone has to be decommissioned first, which cannot be undone. Control Tower enrollment: from an unregistered OU of the same organization, with an AWSControlTowerExecution role trusting the management account and no AWS Config recorder or delivery channel of the account's own; enrolling deploys the baseline StackSets, enables Config and applies the OU's SCPs; existing VPCs are left alone; account-level CloudTrail trails duplicate the organization trail. Verified against https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_accounts_remove.html, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_accounts_invites.html, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_org_delete.html, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/decommission-landing-zone.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/enroll-account.html.

Service-managed StackSets with automatic deployment delete an account's stack instances when it is removed from a target organization or OU, unless RetainStacksOnAccountRemoval is set, in which case the stacks stay and are detached; what happens with automatic deployment off is not documented. Export and Fn::ImportValue are limited to one account and Region and block deleting or changing the exported output while it is imported; Fn::GetStackOutput can cross accounts and Regions through an IAM role and is resolved at create or update time only. The stack name form StackSet-<name>-<id> appears in AWS's examples and is not a documented rule. The Resource Groups Tagging API returns resources that are tagged or were tagged once, never untagged ones; Resource Explorer returns at most the first 1,000 results of a query. Verified against https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/APIReference/API_AutoDeployment.html, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/stacksets-orgs-manage-auto-deployment.html, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-cfn-stack-exports.html, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/intrinsic-function-reference-getstackoutput.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/resourcegroupstagging/latest/APIReference/API_GetResources.html.

limitations: An SCP or RCP that allows an action is not a grant: IAM identity policies, resource policies, permissions boundaries and session policies decide the request and are not evaluated here. The governance-policy evaluation says what the organization forbids, not what the account can do.

Condition keys evaluated with explicit context: aws:RequestedRegion, aws:PrincipalOrgID, aws:PrincipalOrgPaths, aws:PrincipalAccount, aws:PrincipalArn, aws:PrincipalTag/*, aws:PrincipalIsAWSService, aws:ResourceAccount, aws:ResourceOrgID and aws:ResourceOrgPaths, with the organization IDs and paths before and after the move. Other keys, policy variables and unsupported operators are reported as unsupported, never as an allow.

Tag policies: compliance is checked on the sampled resources (existing-resource compliance), enforcement only for the resource types listed in enforced_for (enforcement on supported operations); whether tags are required at creation depends on separate controls (SCP conditions, Config rules) that are not modelled. A tag policy alone never rejects an untagged resource.

RAM: a share that stops reaching the account is a control-plane change; what happens to traffic already flowing is taken from the per-resource-type behaviour model, and data-plane continuity is not tested.
Observed usage comes from the actions the snapshot lists; declared critical operations are evaluated the same way. Anything the account will do that is in neither list is not covered by the verdict.

Workload layer: evaluated from the inventory of the account alone (stacks, a resource sample, the policies read). Resources created outside CloudFormation appear only if the sample returned them; the Tagging API never returns untagged resources and the sample is capped. Of resource policies, bucket policies and role trust policies are read and only for conditions on organization identity; identity policies, KMS key policies and other resource policies are not. Templates are read for references and conditions, not executed, so a value computed at deployment is reported as unknown.
